title: English Language Proficiency Requirement for Fresh Applications for Taxi Driver's Vocational Licence
what_it_is: English Language Proficiency Requirement for Fresh Applications for Taxi Driver's Vocational Licence

sections.label: Taxi driver English proficiency
sections.summary: Taxi drivers need basic English proficiency, shown by GCE O/N level English or Workplace Literacy test, including revoked licence applicants.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Taxi drivers need to have basic proficiency in English to be able to serve their passengers well, as there are locals and foreign visitors who may not understand our local vernacular languages or dialects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: That is why taxi drivers are required to have a GCE “O” or “N” level pass in English, or a Level 3 pass in the Listening, Reading and Speaking modules of the Workplace Literacy-computer Adaptive Test.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Taxi drivers who had their Taxi Driver's Vocational Licences (TDVLs) revoked have to meet prevailing requirements when they apply for a new licence, including language proficiency.

sections.label: English requirement and licence revocation
sections.summary: English proficiency has long been required, with GCE D7 pass from the 1990s and Workplace Literacy test since 2011; revocation grounds are listed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: First of all, it has been a long-standing requirement for TDVL applicants to have basic English language proficiency.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For a more comprehensive and objective assessment of the English proficiency level of the applicants, we have required at least a D7 pass at the GCE "O" level or "N" level in the 1990s.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The Workplace Literacy and Numeracy Assessment, which is in place of relevant certificates like the GCE "O" level, was in place since 2011.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As I have said, this is because the taxi drivers need to communicate effectively with their passengers, who may not be able to speak in the vernacular languages or dialects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Also, let me clarify that for taxi drivers whose TDVL licences are revoked, they are revoked only if they have committed an offence – a court has sentenced them, for instance – or they have been disqualified or suspended from driving for one year or more, or they have accumulated more than 20 demerit points under the Chauffeured Private Hire Car and Taxi Vocational Licence Demerit Points System within 24 months.

sections.label: Appeals to Land Transport Authority
sections.summary: Applicants without documentary proof can appeal to the Land Transport Authority, which assesses each case individually.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: If for some reason they are not able to provide this documentary proof, they can appeal to the Land Transport Authority (LTA) and we will assess this on a case-by-case basis.
